pages.lesson:
LESSON: GUIDED WRITING ORTHOGRAPHY HANDWRITING CLARITY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.6: Guided Writing Orthography Handwriting Clarity

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Guided Writing Orthography Handwriting Clarity. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why should you write clearly?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write common words with the correct orthography
2. create simple sentences using correct structures
3. appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GUIDED WRITING ORTHOGRAPHY HANDWRITING CLARITY
Subject: FRENCH · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Guided Writing Orthography Handwriting Clarity helps you succeed in FRENCH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GUIDED WRITING ORTHOGRAPHY HANDWRITING CLARITY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Write common words with the correct orthography

What this means
In this part you learn to write common words with the correct orthography. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write common words with the correct orthography.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing Orthography Handwriting Clarity”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write common words with the correct orthography. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Create simple sentences using correct structures

What this means
In this part you learn to create simple sentences using correct structures. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: create simple sentences using correct structures.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing Orthography Handwriting Clarity to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can create simple sentences using correct structures. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Guided Writing Orthography Handwriting Clarity is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Guided Writing Orthography Handwriting Clarity”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: write common words with the correct orthography)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Guided Writing Orthography Handwriting Clarity to a partner. (skill: create simple sentences using correct structures)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Guided Writing Orthography Handwriting Clarity to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: write common words with the correct orthography.
3. Practise this skill: create simple sentences using correct structures.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of writing in interactive communication contexts.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Guided Writing Orthography Handwriting Clarity from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Guided Writing Orthography Handwriting Clarity: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Guided Writing Orthography Handwriting Clarity?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why should you write clearly?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Guided Writing Orthography Handwriting Clarity means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: write common words with the correct orthography.
5. Be able to: create simple sentences using correct structures.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
